correctness.rationale: For G of abelian p-power order p^n with conjugate partition r_j, |G[p^j]|=p^{s_j}, hence number of order-p^j cyclic subgroups (p^{s_j}−p^{s_{j−1}})/(p^j−p^{j−1}); each cyclic subgroup has p^{2j}−p^{2j−2} generating ordered pairs. Summation gives p^{2n}θ=1+(p+1)Σ_j p^{j−1+s_{j−1}}(p^{r_j}−1). Each summand is a carry-free run of digit p−1 occupying r_j positions; consecutive starts differ by r_j+1. Rank≥2 implies T≡−1 mod p², numerator≡−p mod p², so reduced denominator p^{2n−1} recovers p,n and digit word recovers partition and invariant factors. Sufficiency follows by constructing that group. Independently tested partitions n=2..9 for primes 2,3,5 and direct sample values 17/32,83/243.
residual_risks: Noncyclic abelian p-groups only; cyclic q=1 is nondiagnostic; cannot extend inverse to arbitrary groups or mixed-prime abelian products.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Chatterjee–Das general cyclic-pair probability paper supplies the Dedekind-psi element-order sum and several rational value bounds, not the complete attainable rational language for abelian p-groups. Amiri/Tărnăuceanu establish fixed-order rigidity of element-order sums; that implies injectivity at fixed order and is NOT new. The submitted strict p-adic denominator and carry-free partition-word condition characterize the entire image with initially unknown prime and group order, a stronger and structurally different inverse statement. No exact covering prior theorem found in searched records; best-of-knowledge only.
residual_risks: Earlier order-sum range results may implicitly encode this digit criterion, although inspected published ones do not supply it as a theorem.
Prime factorization of denominator is part of membership test, not a polynomial-time factoring algorithm.

value.rationale: The set of attainable exact values of a standard random generation invariant is a natural inverse algebraic problem. The proved iff rational-digit language, injectivity across all primes/orders in a noncyclic p-group family, and constructive recovery are reusable for classifying groups from observable probabilities; not merely fixed-order injectivity or a finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Does not classify all finite groups; numerical q can coincide across nonabelian groups, so family restriction is essential.
